key_insight: A physics-informed neural network jointly updates turbine-blade geometry and flow to match prescribed surface-pressure targets.
engineering_relevance: The method enables inverse aerodynamic design by translating desired blade loading into geometric modifications.
method: Constrain the flow with the 2D steady compressible Euler equations.
Optimise differentiable blade surfaces using pressure-target continuation.
Alternate geometry updates with flow re-adaptation.
evidence_signal: On the LS89 cascade with 28 experimental-derived pressure targets, final pressure- and suction-side RMS errors were 1.13% and 2.21% of inlet total pressure; independent SharC verification reproduced principal pressure trends.
watch_item: The 2D inviscid formulation does not resolve viscous or turbulent effects, and verification showed remaining trailing-edge pressure differences.
paper_title: A physics-informed neural network method for pressure-driven turbine-blade optimization
